regions.label: Brain & behaviour
regions.function: Controls sleep, mood, thinking and stress responses. On long missions the brain has to cope with confinement, isolation, disrupted light cycles and high workload.

regions.label: Eyes & vision
regions.function: Vision can change during long-duration spaceflight as body fluids shift toward the head. Report any new blurring or change in sight.

regions.label: Heart & circulation
regions.function: Pumps blood and adapts to gravity. Without gravity, fluids shift and the cardiovascular system can decondition; stress and sleep loss also show up in heart rate and HRV.

regions.label: Lungs & breathing
regions.function: Bring in oxygen and remove CO₂. Cabin atmosphere and dust in closed habitats directly affect breathing.

regions.label: Gut & nutrition
regions.function: Digests food and keeps energy and fluids balanced. Limited, stored food supplies far from Earth make good intake harder.

regions.label: Bones & muscle
regions.function: Support and move the body. In reduced gravity bones and muscles lose strength unless countermeasure exercise is kept up.

regions.label: Immune system & skin
regions.function: Defends against infection. Spaceflight stressors can change immune function; temperature and skin changes are early clues.

regions.label: Whole body & radiation
regions.function: Space radiation passes through the whole body. Exposure is tracked as dose rate and cumulative dose against the mission budget.
